text:
sasha: quick report — discovered a fd leak in py streaming sample when breaking out of async for.

sasha: minimal repro:
```py
it = client.stream_chat(prompt)
async for frame in it:
    if frame['text'].startswith('stop'):
        break
# process exits but socket left open until GC
```

sasha: observed on linux + uvloop; if iterator is cancelled mid-yield underlying socket stays open.

ben: does calling `await it.aclose()` in finally fix it?

sasha: yes, explicit aclose fixes immediately. So this is a wrapper bug — proxy object returned by client doesn't forward aclose/finalizer.

ben: short-term: update quickstart to use `async with client.stream_chat(...) as it:` and add try/finally example. long-term: ensure the proxy forwards `aclose` and implement a finalizer.

sasha: opened issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1623 (py streaming proxy aclose missing + typing note). added repro + suggested fix. @devex-bot add label streaming and py-sdk?

devex-bot: labels "streaming", "py-sdk" added to issue #1623.

sasha: also hitting mypy confusion: sample annotations `-> AsyncIterator[str]` fail when chunks are bytes; propose adding `Chunk = Union[str, bytes, TokenChunk]` alias and TypedDict for chunk shapes. Document in quickstart.

ben: will add small integration test that cancels mid-chunk and asserts fd count returns to baseline. CI should catch regressions.

sre-bot: incident INC-2102 referenced similar pattern; linking for oncall.

sasha: PR incoming that updates docs + sample + test. will tag eng-ml for the wrapper fix.
